# .github/skip-ledger.txt — THE SKIP LEDGER: every reason a test in this tree
# may skip for, and the class of lane that is meant to satisfy it.
#
#   skip <class> <regexp>
#
# A skipped test exits 0, so a lane can go green having run nothing. Two
# readers hold the tree to this file (internal/skipledger):
#
#   * internal/ci (TestEverySkipInTheTreeNamesALedgerReason) reads every
#     t.Skip in the source. A skip with no reason, or a reason no line here
#     matches, is red at the pull request that writes it. A format verb reads
#     as X there, so write a pattern on the reason's fixed words.
#   * tools/gotestreport -skips reads every skip in a lane's `go test -json`
#     record, after the lane ran. A skip with no reason, a reason no line
#     matches, or a reason whose class the lane -provides is red: "no Elixir"
#     in the lane that installs Elixir, SCHEMA_SLOW in a make target that
#     sets SCHEMA_SLOW=1.
#
# The first matching line wins, so a narrow line goes above a broad one. A
# class is a claim about lanes: before adding one, say below which lane
# provides it. Adding a line here never makes a test run; it only says which
# lane is wrong when the test does not.
#
# MEASURED 2026-11-21 on main 8f82586f98 (hetzner2, `go test -json ./...`, no
# SCHEMA_SLOW, which is what the go-test-touched rows run between them): of
# 18,367 tests, 6,759 skip. 6,504 are `slow`, 203 `corpus`, 38 `retired`, 7
# `built`, 6 `env`, 1 `helper`. None gave no reason.

# slow: internal/slowtest.Gate. Provided by every lane that sets
# SCHEMA_SLOW=1 (ci-full.yml's go-test rows, the make leg gates,
# test/slowgate/proof).
skip slow ^SCHEMA_SLOW(: | is unset)

# short: the test is too heavy for -short. Provided by every lane that runs
# without -short.
skip short ^-short: 

# tool:<name>: the test needs a toolchain it did not find. Provided by the
# lane that installs that toolchain. Where a second condition rides along
# (SCHEMA_REQUIRE_CORPUS is unset), the toolchain is still the reason.
skip tool:rust-32bit 32-bit target
skip tool:rust ^rustc (is )?not on PATH
skip tool:rust ^no cargo (toolchain|on PATH)
skip tool:c++ no c\+\+ on PATH
skip tool:c++ ^c\+\+( unavailable| is not on PATH)?(:| and) 
skip tool:c++ clang\+\+
skip tool:c++ ^generated C\+\+ (execution|inclusion) requires
skip tool:c++ ^the generated C\+\+ reader is built with
skip tool:c++ (^no|requires a|: no) C\+\+ compiler
skip tool:cc no cc on PATH
skip tool:cc ^generated C (execution|compilation|syntax check) requires cc
skip tool:cc ^cc( unavailable| not found| is not on PATH)?(: |$)
skip tool:cc ^(requires C compiler|no C compiler on PATH)$
skip tool:cc ^the C compiler .* is absent
skip tool:cc ^the generated C reader is built with cc
skip tool:dotnet ^dotnet (unavailable|not found)
skip tool:dotnet ^no (dotnet on PATH|Roslyn csc\.dll|\.NET ref pack)
skip tool:dotnet ^Unity toolchain unavailable
skip tool:java javac|^java not on PATH|no JDK
skip tool:node ^no node (toolchain|on PATH)
skip tool:eslint ^eslint unavailable
skip tool:dart ^no Dart toolchain
skip tool:dart ^the Dart SDK is not unpacked
skip tool:elixir ^no (Elixir|elixirc):
skip tool:make (requires|shells out to|reads) (the )?make\b
skip tool:make ^no make on PATH
skip tool:git shells out to git
skip tool:sh ^no sh on PATH
skip tool:sbcl ^sbcl not installed
skip tool:go ^go: 

# sibling: a serialize runtime checkout is not staged beside the tree.
# Provided by every lane that clones the sibling runtimes at their pins.
skip sibling ^serialize(\.(h|c|cs|js|rs))?\b.*(not staged|not found|not installed|unavailable|not at)
skip sibling ^named as not run: (the sibling serialize|serialize\.c)
skip sibling ^no serialize\.(js|rs) runtime
skip sibling ^the C# runtime checkout is not at

# corpus: the C++ reference's fixed-form corpus (build/fixedform-corpus) is
# not built. Provided by every lane that builds it first (make
# tables-fixedform-corpus; SCHEMA_REQUIRE_CORPUS=1 turns the skip into a
# failure there).
skip corpus (byte oracle|corpus|oracle) is (not built|absent)
skip corpus ^no fixed-form corpus at
skip corpus ^fixedform[- ]corpus (not built|unavailable)
skip corpus ^the tree carries no corpus manifest

# built: the test reads an artifact a make target builds. Provided by the
# lane that runs that target.
skip built ^run make \S+ to build
skip built is written by `make tables-lists`
skip built is not built: (run )?make 

# env: the test runs only when a make target or a person sets its variable.
# Provided by the lane that sets it.
skip env ^set SCHEMA_[A-Z0-9_]+
skip env ^certify tier: set SCHEMA_CERTIFY_INT32_MAX=1
skip env ^SCHEMA_MOO_FIXED_BENCH unset
skip env requires CARDS_UPDATE_(FIXTURE|CORPUS)=1$
skip env runs? under make tables-cs-fixed-roadmap$

# nightly: a campaign too long for a commit. Provided by the nightly workflow
# that runs it.
skip nightly nightly (only|campaign)

# tag: the test is for another build-tag configuration. Provided by the lane
# that builds under that tag (ci-full.yml's leg-tagged job).
skip tag schema_leg_python build tag$
skip tag ^this build registers .* the pages state the default build$

# platform: the host cannot do what the test needs (symlinks, POSIX modes, a
# Linux-only signal). Provided by every Linux lane.
skip platform symlink
skip platform POSIX
skip platform on Linux( only)?$
skip platform ^Linux CI artifact contract$
skip platform ^platform has no kernel address-space ceiling$

# root: the test proves nothing as root. Provided by a lane that does not run
# as root.
skip root ^root writes (through|into) a read-only (directory|file)
skip root ^root reads through a directory it may not search

# volume:aliases: the test needs a volume that takes two spellings of a name
# (a case fold, a Unicode normalization) for one entry, as APFS on macOS
# does. Provided by no CI lane today: every Linux lane keeps the spellings
# apart, so these tests run on macOS hosts only (the Studio, the macOS
# benches). Their controls, which need the spellings kept apart, are
# platform skips above and run on every Linux lane.
skip volume:aliases ^this (volume|file system) keeps .+ apart, so 

# helper: a helper-process entry point, run by the test that names it.
# Provided by no lane: it skips whenever go test runs it directly.
skip helper TestGooseDieWithParent
skip helper ^helper for Test

# inapplicable: a table-driven test's row does not apply to this case.
# Provided by no lane.
skip inapplicable ^§3\.3 is a fixed table's
skip inapplicable ^the tool writes no cook for
skip inapplicable ^the Lua table backend does not generate this unit
skip inapplicable ^the pointers corpus declares no variable-length root$
skip inapplicable ^reference (refuses the wire|has no cook)
skip inapplicable ^no fixed/ufixed root field over seeds
skip inapplicable ^docs/SPEC-TABLES\.md §3\.4 does not list
skip inapplicable ^a sibling C\+\+ serialize checkout at .* resolves SERIALIZE
skip inapplicable records with no capacity \(schema-fixedproof-x1's row\)
skip inapplicable ^FirstV3ModuleTag is unset: 

# retired, unported: THE TEST RUNS IN NO LANE. Each names the document that
# owes it. Provided by no lane: these lines are the count of what is owed,
# not a permission (38 retired tests on 2026-11-21).
skip retired re-pin as a verdict: docs/plans/strict-only\.md$
skip retired ^retired by docs/
skip retired ^the wide-text unit is retired$
skip unported ^UNPORTED

# tool:other: a toolchain named only at run time ("<tool>: exec: ... not
# found"). Last, so every named toolchain above is matched first.
skip tool:other executable file not found
skip tool:other ^(building a multi-byte-point locale requires localedef|the ps_AF locale source is not installed|localedef could not build the locale)
skip tool:other ^(\S+ is not on PATH|no \S+ on PATH|none of .* is on PATH|\S+ unavailable)(: |$)
